split: No training split; a new prompt benchmark built from 12 animals, 12 objects and 11 colors, evaluated on Stable Diffusion. This subset uses the template "a [animalA] and a [animalB]", 66 prompts. Side comparison with Prompt-to-Prompt uses 20 randomly selected prompts per subset; user study uses 10 randomly selected prompts per subset.
split_quote: This results in 66 Animal-Animal and Object-Object pairs and 144 Animal-Object pairs.
count: 66 prompts, 64 images per prompt from 64 random seeds applied across all methods. User study: 65 respondents, 10 prompts, the same 4 seeds for all methods. Prompt-to-Prompt comparison: 20 prompts per subset (images per prompt not stated).
count_quote: For each prompt, we then generate 64 images using 64 random seeds applied across all methods.

dataset: Complex prompts from StructureDiffusion and Conceptual Captions
split: No training split; 40 prompts collected from the qualitative examples in the StructureDiffusion paper and the Conceptual Captions dataset, evaluated on Stable Diffusion against StructureDiffusion.
split_quote: We collected 40 prompts extracted from the qualitative examples in the StructureDiffusion paper [Feng et al. 2022], and the Conceptual Captions dataset [Sharma et al. 2018].
count: 40 prompts; the same 64 random seeds for all methods (images per prompt not printed in this passage).
count_quote: We compare our method against both StructureDiffusion and Stable Diffusion and use the same 64 random seeds for all methods.

dataset: User study prompts, lowest-performing prompt for Attend-and-Excite
split: User study prompts: 10 randomly selected prompts per subset, the same 4 randomly selected seeds for all methods. Which prompt was lowest-performing is not identified beyond its vote share.
split_quote: We randomly select 10 prompts from each subset and apply the same 4 randomly-selected seeds to all methods.
count: 65 respondents; the quoted figure is one prompt's vote share (59.09% for Attend-and-Excite, 16% each for SD and StructureDiffusion).
count_quote: Even our lowest performing prompt received 59.09% of votes (with SD and StructureDiffusion tied for second, each receiving 16% of votes).

split: No dataset; runtime measurement only, evaluated on an A100 GPU.
split_quote: Evaluated on an A100 GPU, Stable Diffusion generates a single image in approximately 5.6 seconds.
count: Approximate seconds for a single image; number of timed images or repeats not stated.
count_quote: Evaluated on an A100 GPU, Stable Diffusion generates a single image in approximately 5.6 seconds.

split: Base model and coordinators trained on the Slakh2100 training set (1,500 tracks); coordinator trained on 48 s tracks (Ltrain = 5), evaluated on 4l (48 s) and 10l (120 s) tracks (Ltest = 13); FAD is computed against middle parts cut from the training dataset tracks of the same length.
split_quote: This dataset contains 1,500 tracks in the training set, each consisting of four different stems: Bass, Drums, Guitar, and Piano.
count: 128 generated tracks per reported FAD value; the paper notes 128 vs 1,024 tracks changes FAD by a small margin.
count_quote: To decrease GPU usage, we settled on using 128 tracks in our reported metric values.

split: Base model trained on the CLEVR dataset (30,000 images, 128x128 downsampled to 64x64) with one conditioning; coordinator trained with up to 2 conditionings, evaluated with up to 5 conditionings on randomly generated position sets.
split_quote: During training, the coordinator observed conditioning objects of size up to Ltrain = 2.
count: 256 random sets of positions per number of conditionings, one generated image per set (256 generated samples per accuracy).
count_quote: For each of the 256 samples generated during evaluation, we generated positions

split: Dataset of 7,300 map and satellite image pairs collected with the Google Maps API; coordinator trained on N = 96, evaluated at N = 96 and out-of-distribution N = 128. A held-out train/test split of the 7,300 pairs is not stated; FID is against the whole dataset.
split_quote: We train the coordinator on size N × N , where N = 96, and perform evaluation for out-of-distribution sampling with N = 128.
count: 3,072 generated samples compared with the whole 7,300-image satellite dataset.
count_quote: When reporting the FID metric for a given model, we compare the whole satellite dataset, containing 7,300 images, with 3,072 generated samples.

split: No training; MultiDiffusion applied to a pretrained Stable Diffusion; for each text prompt the reference set is N images of 512x512 from the base model, compared with 512x512 crops of generated panoramas, repeated for 8 text prompts.
split_quote: That is, for a given text prompt, we sample N different 512 × 512 images from Φ, and consider them as our reference dataset.
count: N = 2000 generated panoramas (one random 512x512 crop each) per prompt, repeated over 8 text prompts.
count_quote: We used N = 2000 samples and repeated this evaluation for 8 different text-conditioning.

split: No training; evaluated on a subset of the COCO validation set with 2 to 4 foreground objects, excluding people and masks occupying less than 5% of the image.
split_quote: We apply our method on a subset from the validation set, obtained by filtering examples which consists of 2 to 4 foreground objects, excluding people, and masks that occupy less than 5% of the image.
count: 1K samples (one per COCO validation example in the subset); images per example not stated.
count_quote: This results in 1K diverse samples.
